name: Web search
description: Searches with no setup and no key: with nothing saved it asks Wikipedia (the top 5 articles, each with its title, a one-line snippet and its address), which is not the whole web and has no news. With the address of a SearXNG you run yourself, on this computer or your home network, it searches the web and news through that instead, the top 8 each. It does not use a public SearXNG or ask any search company directly, does not search images, does not open or read the pages it finds, and does not install or run SearXNG for you.
author: Cypher Sisters

tools.web_search: Search Wikipedia, or the owner's own SearXNG if one is saved, and get the top results. With none saved: Wikipedia only, not the whole web, top 5, private details taken out of the words first. With one saved: the web through that SearXNG, top 8, never Wikipedia. Only the search words are sent.
tools.news_search: Search recent news through the owner's own SearXNG and get the top 8 stories: the title, a one-line snippet, the address and the engine that found it. With no SearXNG saved it says it needs one: Wikipedia has no news.
tools.search_settings: What web search asks: Wikipedia, or the saved SearXNG address and whether it answers right now.
tools.set_address: Save the address of the owner's own SearXNG, like http://192.168.1.20:8888 or http://127.0.0.1:8888. Only an address on this computer or the home network is taken; a public SearXNG is refused. For an address off this computer, the bot raises a Yes card for that address and port.

web_search: search the web for how to store fresh basil
look up when the Eiffel Tower was built
news_search: what's in the news about the Mars mission
search the news for storm damage in our county
search_settings: which search box does web search use
set_address: set my SearXNG address to http://192.168.1.20:8888

consent: Web search works with no setup. With no SearXNG address saved, when you ask for a search it sends the words you asked it to search for, after private details are taken out, to en.wikipedia.org, and your internet address goes with them like any web request. Nothing else about you. If you save the address of your own SearXNG, that address stays in its own data folder on this computer, and your search words go only to that SearXNG, never to Wikipedia, and nothing else about you. SearXNG then asks search engines on the internet itself (outside this package): they see the words but no cookies, account or device details from you, and like any web request they see the internet address SearXNG uses, which is your home's address when SearXNG runs at home. Search words and results are not stored.
